title: observability: token-level cost/latency dashboard improvements + alert tuning
author: Aisha Patel
description: Add more robust token-level cost and latency metrics, improve dashboard ergonomics for runtime and Dedicated customers, and reduce alert noise by tuning thresholds and introducing adaptive burn-rate detection. Motivation: token-level observability is critical for debugging regressions and cost spikes; recent incidents (INC-2026-02-hot-path) showed gaps in alert sensitivity and lack of sampling in traces. This PR implements: 1) new token-level metrics (per-route tokens, token gen latency percentiles, token CPU/GPU cost estimates) exported from the serving runtime and aggregated in the telemetry pipeline; 2) dashboard updates with heatmaps, per-route breakdown panels, and an application-level cost slab view for quicker triage; 3) alert tuning: replace a single static threshold with a two-stage approach (low-sensitivity warnings + high-sensitivity escalations) and a short-window burn-rate detector to catch sudden cost/latency spikes without triggering noisy infra-level alerts; 4) tracing improvements: add token-sequence tags and introduce sampling controls to ensure traces are representative without overwhelming storage; 5) tests and migration notes for customers using Dedicated/private deployments. Checklist: - [x] runtime metric instrumentation - [x] telemetry ingestion + aggregator mapping - [x] dashboards and docs - [x] alert rules + runbook updates - [x] unit + e2e smoke tests - [x] Linear: ENG-1842, ENG-1901. See commits summary and changed files for details.
